1	## Problem and disagreements
2	
3	<!-- slice: requirements -->
4	The requirements (`requirements.md`, prompt; spec `attachments/order-tracking-spec.md`:1-21; ledger C-1..C-5) ask for: carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2), every change stored per order (spec:7-8); `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9); an email on every status change via an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4); per-order opt-out from a link in any tracking email, no sign-in (spec:12-13); plus guest orders trackable via the link in their order confirmation email (prompt). Statuses: label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception (C-3).
5	
6	Disagreements and gaps against the code and docs:
7	- The repo has no order concept at all. `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`; there is no HTTP framework, no persistence, no `/orders` route. "GET /orders/{id} shows the latest status" (spec:9) therefore describes a new endpoint on an order resource that does not exist yet; checkout (F2, `docs/product/prd.md:22`, roadmap Q4 `docs/product/roadmap.md:3`) is what would create orders and is not built. Order tracking is roadmap Q1 (`roadmap.md:4`), after checkout.
8	- The "order confirmation email" the guest addition relies on is not in any PRD feature: checkout R1/R2 (`features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`) mention no confirmation email, and order-tracking R2 covers status-change emails only (`features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`). No guest/account model exists in PRD or code; the PRD personas only list Shopper and Merchant (`prd.md:9-10`).
9	- PRD order-tracking R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); spec item 2 and its AC expose only the latest status. History is stored (spec:8) but no criterion exposes it.
10	- PRD R3 "carrier updates move an order's status" (`order-tracking/prd.md:15`) vs. the spec's separate shipment status: the spec calls it "shipment status" (spec:9,10,18), the PRD "an order's status". Whether shipment status is a new field alongside an existing order status (none exists in code) or the order status itself is unsettled.
11	- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider: `docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10` has only Shopper, shop, Payments gateway; `lld/flows.md:3` has only checkout. The change adds two external actors inbound (carriers) and one outbound (email API), a C4 context change for the impact lanes.
12	- Spec says "two shipping carriers" (spec:7) without naming them; C-2 gives the auth model (shared secret per carrier) but not payload formats, signature algorithm, or secret provisioning.
13	- The prompt's addition (guest orders, no account) interacts with spec AC "GET /orders/{id}": a guest has no sign-in, so the read path needs an unguessable link token; the spec's endpoint says nothing about authorisation. The opt-out link (spec:12-13) has the same no-sign-in need.
14	
15	## Features
16	
17	<!-- slice: requirements -->
18	- Run feature: `order-tracking` (C-1; `requirements.md` `## Refined` `feature: order-tracking`). It matches PRD F3 "Order tracking" (`docs/product/prd.md:23`), `features/order-tracking/prd.md`. No correction needed.
19	- Features touched besides it: F2 checkout (creates orders, and the confirmation email the guest link depends on; `prd.md:22`) is a dependency in effect although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` says "Dependencies: None". F4 order management (`prd.md:24`; refund/export, `order-management/prd.md:13-14`) reads the same order resource but is not changed. The living analysis `docs/product/features/order-tracking/analysis/README.md` does not exist (folder holds only `prd.md`), so there is no prior analysis and nothing to reuse.
20	- Candidate contexts (for the synthesis to settle): (1) Shipment status ingestion — carrier webhooks, signature check, per-order history; PRD R3. (2) Order tracking view — `GET /orders/{id}` latest status (and history, R1) incl. guest access by link; PRD R1. (3) Tracking notifications — status-change emails, opt-out per order; PRD R2. Guest access may be its own context or part of (2)/(3), depending on whether a guest token is shared; the impact lanes decide.
21	
22	## Acceptance-criteria review
23	
24	<!-- slice: requirements -->
25	The ticketless spec has four unnumbered criteria (spec:17-21); labelled here S-1..S-4 in order. C-5: they stand as written, so every rewrite is a proposal only.
26	
27	- S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." Ambiguous: "accepted" has no observable failure side (invalid signature, unknown order, unknown status, duplicate or out-of-order delivery), and nothing says the signature is verified though C-2 requires it. Testable only for the happy path.
28	- S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." Ambiguous: "latest" = most recently received or most recent by carrier event time (webhooks can arrive out of order); response shape and the no-updates-yet case unstated; authorisation for guests unstated. Contradicted by code only in that the endpoint and order do not exist.
29	- S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." Ambiguous: a repeated same-status webhook is not a change; whether every one of the five statuses emails (spec:10 says "whenever", PRD R2 "every status change"); who the recipient is for a guest order (the order's email). Delivery failure behaviour unstated.
30	- S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." Testable as written for emails after opt-out; missing: the opt-out link works without sign-in (spec:13) and is in every tracking email, is per order only, and that opt-out does not suppress other orders' emails. Also unclear whether the confirmation email is a "tracking email".
31	- Missing M-1: guest orders (prompt) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email — no spec criterion exists.
32	- Missing M-2: webhook authentication — a status update with an invalid or missing per-carrier signature is rejected and stores nothing (C-2).
33	- Missing M-3: history — every change is kept per order (spec:8; PRD R1 "history"); no criterion states it, and no endpoint shows it.
34	- Missing M-4: only the five statuses of C-3 are accepted; an update naming another status is rejected.
35	- Missing M-5: idempotent/out-of-order handling of repeated webhooks (carriers retry).
36	
37	Rewrites are in group (c).
38	
39	## Risks
40	
41	<!-- slice: requirements -->
42	- Hard dependency on unbuilt functionality: no order model, no HTTP layer, no checkout, no confirmation email (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `README.md:5-8`, roadmap `roadmap.md:3-4`). The analysis must say what this change creates versus assumes; delivering tracking before checkout means tracking has no orders to track. Evidence: above.
43	- Security of the unauthenticated surfaces: webhook endpoint (signature, replay) and guest link/opt-out link (token guessability, enumeration of `GET /orders/{id}` by sequential id). Evidence: C-2, spec:12-13, prompt addition.
44	- Webhook out-of-order/duplicate delivery can regress "latest" status (e.g. delivered then in_transit) and send wrong emails (spec:9-10).
45	- Email provider unchosen (C-4): vendor lock-in is avoided by treating it as an outbound HTTP API, but delivery failures, retries and rate limits are unspecified; emailing synchronously within the webhook request threatens NFR1 p95 under 300 ms (`prd.md:28`).
46	- Privacy: emailing shoppers and the guest address handling; opt-out is legally relevant for marketing mail but tracking mail is transactional — wording of the opt-out criterion matters. No PRD statement on retention.
47	- NFR2 coverage 90% (`prd.md:29`) applies to all new code.
48	- Scope fork: PRD order-tracking R1 "history" vs. spec "latest" (see disagreements).
49	
50	<!-- slice: repo -->
51	- Greenfield: no web framework, routing, persistence, order model, config or dependency exists (src/shop/__init__.py:1-9, pyproject.toml:1-6). The planner must choose or find these elsewhere; this is not a small attach.
52	- Security-sensitive paths, new: webhook signature verification with a per-carrier secret (secret storage/config has no home yet); unauthenticated opt-out and guest-tracking links need unguessable per-order tokens (spec :12-13). Load-bearing surfaces: the webhook intake and the token links.
53	- Webhook semantics: duplicate/out-of-order deliveries affect "latest status" vs history (spec :7-9); no ordering rule in the sources.
54	- Email provider unchosen and outbound call can fail; sending in the webhook request path couples carrier ack to provider availability (answer 3).
55	- Dependency: guest and registered order data and a confirmation email do not exist in code; PRD for checkout is placeholder text (checkout PRD :13-14).
56	- Test suite is tiny and fast; no flaky suites observed.
57	
58	## Changes since the last analysis
59	
60	<!-- slice: requirements -->
61	Not applicable: no previous analysis and no living analysis for `order-tracking` exist (`docs/product/features/order-tracking/` holds only `prd.md`).
62	
63	## Questions for the user
64	
65	<!-- slice: requirements -->
66	The user cannot answer during this run; the coordinator may record the defaults in group (b) and the proposals in group (c) as assumptions.
67	
68	### (a) Open questions
69	- A-1 Order and confirmation email prerequisites: no order model, confirmation email or guest identity exists in the repo or the PRD. Does this change create a minimal order record and confirmation-email link, or assume checkout (F2) delivers them? Proceed on: tracking assumes an order record with id, customer email and optional account id provided by checkout, and the analysis lists the minimal contract it needs from it; not a blocker for the analysis, but the plan sequencing depends on it.
70	- A-2 Carrier webhook contract: names of the two carriers, payload format, signature algorithm, and how a carrier's event is matched to an order (tracking number/order reference). Proceed on: one generic payload `{order reference, status, event time}` with an HMAC signature header per carrier, flagged as an assumption; per-carrier adapters are a seam.
71	
72	### (b) Conventional defaults
73	- B-1 Assumed: "latest status" is the one with the most recent carrier event time, ties by receipt order — confirm or correct (webhook retries, out-of-order delivery).
74	- B-2 Assumed: duplicate webhook of the same status for the same order stores nothing new and sends no email — confirm or correct.
75	- B-3 Assumed: a webhook with an invalid signature returns 401 and stores nothing; unknown order or unknown status returns 4xx and stores nothing — confirm or correct (common webhook convention).
76	- B-4 Assumed: guest tracking and opt-out links carry an unguessable random token per order; the link is the credential and no sign-in is required — confirm or correct.
77	- B-5 Assumed: emails are sent after the update is stored (not blocking the webhook response); a send failure does not roll back the stored update — confirm or correct (NFR1, `prd.md:28`).
78	- B-6 Assumed: the opt-out applies to status-change emails of that order only, not to the order confirmation email, and is not reversible in this scope — confirm or correct.
79	- B-7 Assumed: `GET /orders/{id}` exposes latest status only, as the spec says; history is stored and exposed later (PRD R1 "history" left open) — confirm or correct.
80	
81	### (c) Proposed refined acceptance criteria (proposals only; C-5)
82	- S-1 -> "A status update from a carrier carrying a valid signature for that carrier's secret, naming a known order and one of label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception, is accepted (2xx) and appended to that order's status history with its carrier, status and event time; an update with an invalid or missing signature, an unknown order or an unknown status is rejected (4xx) and stores nothing."
83	- S-2 -> "GET /orders/{id} returns the order's latest shipment status (greatest event time) and its event time; an order with no updates yet returns an explicit 'no shipment status' value; a guest order is readable with its link token and without sign-in, and a request with neither a valid token nor an authorised account is refused."
84	- S-3 -> "When an accepted update changes an order's latest shipment status, an email naming the new status and the opt-out link is sent to the order's email address; an update repeating the current status, or an older update that does not change the latest status, sends no email."
85	- S-4 -> "Following the opt-out link in any tracking email, without signing in, records an opt-out for that order only; afterwards no further tracking email is sent for that order, while tracking emails for the buyer's other orders continue."
86	- M-1 (new) -> "A guest order (placed without an account) is trackable through the link in its order confirmation email, with no sign-in."
87	- M-2 covered in S-1 rewrite; M-4 covered in S-1 rewrite; M-5 covered in S-1/S-3 rewrite (duplicates and out-of-order).
88	- M-3 (new) -> "Every accepted status update is kept per order and none is overwritten." (exposure of history through an endpoint is left to A/B-7.)
89	
90	### (d) The feature
91	- `features` stays `order-tracking` (C-1); no correction. Note F2 checkout is a de-facto dependency not listed under `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23`; proposed as a PRD note, not a ticket write. Proposed slugs: none needed.
92	
93	<!-- slice: repo -->

96	_None._ (Persistence, framework and where orders live are not in the repository; they are implementation choices for the planner, recorded as risks above.)

Read this before the analysis draft is written — the analyst in its `draft`

each context file's exact front matter and headings, what each section

The `draft` pass writes a folder for people first: plain-word headings, short
sections, a README someone can read without opening anything else. Every file
name is `README.md` or kebab-case `.md` made of plain words (no `index.md`, no
subfolder, nothing else). The analysis is read by machines as well as people:
the README's front matter (`ready_for_planning` above all, which

else: EXACTLY this front matter and these six headings, in this order:

1	# /acs:analyze-requirements — the analysis templates
2	
3	Read this before the analysis draft is written — the analyst in its `draft`
4	pass, and the coordinator when the `draft` action is due: the README's and
5	each context file's exact front matter and headings, what each section
6	carries, how the files are written, and the load-bearing surfaces the Risks
7	must name. The survey and the synthesis need none of it.
8	
9	## The folder
10	
11	The `draft` pass writes a folder for people first: plain-word headings, short
12	sections, a README someone can read without opening anything else. Every file
13	name is `README.md` or kebab-case `.md` made of plain words (no `index.md`, no
14	subfolder, nothing else). The analysis is read by machines as well as people:
15	the README's front matter (`ready_for_planning` above all, which
16	`/acs:create-impl-plan` reads) is part of the deliverable, not decoration. Emit
17	exactly these keys, with
18	these types, and exactly these headings in this order (the task's
19	`<constraint name="mode">` and `<constraint name="feature">` say which front
20	matter applies).
21	
22	The folder holds two kinds of file.
23	
24	## The README — `README.md`
25	
26	**The README** — `README.md`, readable on its own by someone who opens nothing
27	else: EXACTLY this front matter and these six headings, in this order:
28	
29	```markdown
30	---
31	ticket: SHOP-123
32	ready_for_planning: true
33	---
34	
35	# Analysis — SHOP-123: Accept CSV imports over 10 MB
36	
37	## Scope and summary
38	## Contexts
39	## Refined acceptance criteria
40	## Cross-cutting risks and decisions
41	## Questions and assumptions
42	## Verdict
43	```
44	
45	- **Front matter.** `ticket` is the ticket id; a run with no ticket writes
46	  `feature: <slug>` in its place. `ready_for_planning` is the
47	  verdict below, as a boolean. Never invent another key and never omit one of
48	  the two — except that a Discovery draft (`mode` discovery: the feature's
49	  living analysis) opens with the ADR-0122 version keys before them: `status:
50	  proposed`, `version` (the living analysis's `version` + 1, or `1` when there
51	  is none), `tickets` (carried over from the living analysis, `[]` when there
52	  is none) and `feature`. There is no `api_surface` key (ADR-0134) and no
53	  `needs_design_recommendation` (ADR-0139): an older analysis that still
54	  carries one is read with the key ignored, and none is written. The analysis
55	  never judges whether a design is needed.
56	- **`## Scope and summary`** — the requirements in terms of this repository,
57	  in a few sentences: the behaviour that changes, for whom, what "done"
58	  means, and what is out of scope. Name every disagreement between the
59	  requirements' prose and the code, each citing the file that contradicts it.
60	- **`## Contexts`** — a table, one row per context file, linked by its bare
61	  file name (no `/`, no anchor); every context file is listed, and only those
62	  — the controller refuses a link that does not resolve and a context file
63	  the table does not list:
64	
65	  | Context | File | Purpose |
66	  | --- | --- | --- |
67	  | CSV import | [csv-import.md](csv-import.md) | how an uploaded file becomes rows |
68	
69	- **`## Refined acceptance criteria`** — every criterion of the
70	  requirements, quoted with its `AC-n`, marked `testable` / `ambiguous` /
71	  `untestable` / `contradicted` / `missing`, with the rewrite for each
72	  non-clean entry and its state: `confirmed (C-n)` when the user confirmed it
73	  and the coordinator recorded it (`requirements refine`, which also amends
74	  the ticket when there is one) — quote it as `requirements.md`'s
75	  `## Refined` now carries it; `rejected (C-n)`; or `proposed — open (C-n)`
76	  when unanswered. Never present an unconfirmed
77	  rewrite as applied. Name the context file(s) each criterion lands in.
78	- **`## Cross-cutting risks and decisions`** — only what spans contexts or
79	  the whole change: the interfaces it adds or alters (each named, or "none" —
80	  an interface change is designed with `/acs:create-api-contract`) with
81	  their reason, a risk two contexts share, a load-bearing surface (each linked to the context
82	  file that details it). One-context risks stay in that context file.
83	- **`## Questions and assumptions`** — one line per clarification entry, by
84	  its `C-n` id and status (`open`, `answered`, `assumed`), with the question
85	  and the answer, or the rationale when assumed. Every item of the notes'
86	  `## Questions for the user` appears here as its `C-n`; the ledger
87	  (`clarifications.json`) is the source of truth. Then the assumptions: only
88	  what the user did not answer, with why each is needed and what breaks if it
89	  is wrong (a ledger entry with `--source assumption` included). A default
90	  the user confirmed is an answer, not an assumption. `_None recorded._` when
91	  there are none.
92	- **`## Verdict`** — `ready_for_planning: true` or `false`, in prose, with the
93	  reason. `false` requires naming exactly what is missing and which open
94	  question would settle it — and the question must be one where every
95	  default could build the wrong thing (a contradiction with the code, a
96	  design document or an ADR; a behaviour the criteria depend on that nothing
97	  defines; a fork in scope). A detail with a conventional default — "prints"
98	  means stdout, a credential check is exact and case-sensitive, argument
99	  counts the requirements never mention are out of scope — is never a reason for
100	  `false`: the user confirmed or corrected it, or, unanswered, it is an
101	  assumption recorded in `## Questions and assumptions` with a proposed
102	  criterion rewrite.
103	
104	## One file per context — `<context>.md`
105	
106	**One file per context** — `<context>.md`, one per context of the notes'
107	`## Contexts`, named by its file name there: a kebab-case name made of plain
108	words (never `index.md`, no subfolder), with EXACTLY this front matter and
109	these five headings, in this order:
110	
111	```markdown
112	---
113	context: csv-import
114	---
115	
116	# CSV import
117	
118	## Impact map
119	## Rules and edge cases
120	## Risks
121	## Open questions
122	## API notes
123	```
124	
125	- **Front matter.** `context` is the file name without `.md`. A Discovery
126	  draft adds, after `context`, `feature`, `status: proposed`, `version` and
127	  `tickets` — the same values as the README.
128	- **`## Impact map`** — a table, and its FIRST column is a repo-relative path,
129	  because that column is how a reader sees what this change actually touches:
130	
131	  | Path | Component | Change | Evidence |
132	  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
133	  | `src/import/api.py` | import API | new size branch on upload | `api.py:88` rejects >10 MB today |
134	  | `tests/test_import_api.py` | import API tests | new cases for the large-file path | covers `upload()` at `:41` |
135	
136	  Source, tests, docs and configuration all belong here. Every row carries
137	  evidence you read. A file the change CREATES is a row too, marked as new.
138	- **`## Rules and edge cases`** — the business rules this context enforces
139	  that the change touches, and the edge cases a test must cover, each cited.
140	- **`## Risks`** — implementation and shipping risks in this context with
141	  their evidence and, where one exists, the mitigation the implementation
142	  plan should consider; a load-bearing surface named with its paths.
143	- **`## Open questions`** — the `C-n` entries that concern this context only,
144	  by id and status (the README holds the full list), or `_None._`.
145	- **`## API notes`** — the surface this context adds or changes (endpoint,
146	  flag, message, schema), cited, or `_None._`.
147	
148	A context file never restates another's rows, rules or risks: it links to the
149	file that owns them (`see [payment-refunds.md](payment-refunds.md)`).
150	
151	## Without a ticket, and on a Discovery run
152	
153	On a run with no ticket the README's first key is `feature: <slug>` in place of `ticket:`, and its title
154	reads `# Analysis — <feature>: <subject>`. A Discovery run's draft — the
155	feature's living analysis — opens the README with the version keys of
156	ADR-0122 before the three above: `status: proposed`, `version` (the living
157	analysis's `version` + 1, or `1` for the feature's first analysis), `tickets`
158	(carried over from the living analysis) and `feature`; each context file then
159	carries `feature` and the same three version keys after `context`:
160	
161	```yaml
162	---
163	status: proposed
164	version: 2
165	tickets: ["SHOP-120"]
166	feature: wishlist
167	ready_for_planning: true
168	---
169	```
170	
171	## What the review holds the draft to
172	
173	This skill is where the requirements' ambiguities are SUPPOSED to surface, so the
174	README's `## Questions and assumptions` and the ledger are the same set of
175	facts in two places: every question is a ledger entry, and that section names
176	each entry by its `C-n` id and its status, so the next skill can see what is
177	still open. A question that concerns one context only is also listed in that
178	context file's `## Open questions`, by the same `C-n`.
179	
180	What each section carries is defined above; the
181	contract that matters here is that every context file's `## Impact map` is a
182	table whose first column is a repo-relative path (that column is what the
183	load-bearing-surface step below reads), that the README's front-matter values
184	agree with the sections beneath them, and that the answers show: the README's
185	`## Questions and assumptions` lists every `C-n` with its answer or status and
186	holds as assumptions only what the user did not answer, and
187	`## Refined acceptance criteria` states which criteria were confirmed into the
188	requirements (and so the ticket, when there is one). Keep every section short;
189	an empty one says `_None._`. The README summarizes and links — it never
190	copies a context file's rows.
191	
192	## Writing the files
193	
194	The analyst writes and revises every file through Bash with acs's own
195	writer — `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/acs.py" write <path>
196	<<'ACS_EOF'`, the file's content, then `ACS_EOF` alone on the last line; an
197	in-place revision reads the file and writes it whole again the same way —
198	never through the Write or Edit tool. The draft lives in acs's workspace,
199	in the main checkout (ADR-0136), where a session in a worktree is refused
200	any Write/Edit; and the runtime also refuses a subagent's Write/Edit of a
201	file named like a report ("Subagents should return findings as text, not
202	write report files"), so each attempt would be a turn lost before the same
203	content lands via Bash anyway.
204	
205	## Load-bearing surfaces — name them in the context's `## Risks`
206	
207	The impact map is the first place anyone can see WHAT this change touches, and
208	that is the single strongest input to the delivery-path judgement /acs:ship
209	makes later from the plan (ADR-0095). Nothing here writes a rigor setting —
210	there is no `stakes` axis any more, and this skill does not classify — but the
211	analysis is where the evidence for that judgement is recorded.
212	
213	So when the impact map reaches a surface the repo treats as load-bearing —
214	authentication or authorization, payments, a migration or any stored shape, a
215	public API other systems call, concurrency or ordering, anything the repo's own
216	architecture docs flag — say so explicitly in that context file's `## Risks`, naming the paths, and
217	list it again, linked, under the README's `## Cross-cutting risks and
218	decisions`. A
219	risk entry that names a boundary is read by `/acs:create-impl-plan` (which
220	carries it into the plan's own Risks section) and then by whoever judges the
221	path, and it is what turns a one-file change into a `standard` or `complex`
222	run instead of a `trivial` one.
223	
224	Prose, not a setting: what makes this work is that the risk is stated where a
225	reader will weigh it, not that a glob matched.

2	
3	<!-- slice: requirements -->
4	The requirements (`requirements.md`, prompt; spec `attachments/order-tracking-spec.md`:1-21; ledger C-1..C-5) ask for: carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2), every change stored per order (spec:7-8); `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9); an email on every status change via an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4); per-order opt-out from a link in any tracking email, no sign-in (spec:12-13); plus guest orders trackable via the link in their order confirmation email (prompt). Statuses: label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception (C-3).
5	
6	Disagreements and gaps against the code and docs:
7	- The repo has no order concept at all. `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`; there is no HTTP framework, no persistence, no `/orders` route. "GET /orders/{id} shows the latest status" (spec:9) therefore describes a new endpoint on an order resource that does not exist yet; checkout (F2, `docs/product/prd.md:22`, roadmap Q4 `docs/product/roadmap.md:3`) is what would create orders and is not built. Order tracking is roadmap Q1 (`roadmap.md:4`), after checkout.
8	- The "order confirmation email" the guest addition relies on is not in any PRD feature: checkout R1/R2 (`features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`) mention no confirmation email, and order-tracking R2 covers status-change emails only (`features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`). No guest/account model exists in PRD or code; the PRD personas only list Shopper and Merchant (`prd.md:9-10`).
9	- PRD order-tracking R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); spec item 2 and its AC expose only the latest status. History is stored (spec:8) but no criterion exposes it.
10	- PRD R3 "carrier updates move an order's status" (`order-tracking/prd.md:15`) vs. the spec's separate shipment status: the spec calls it "shipment status" (spec:9,10,18), the PRD "an order's status". Whether shipment status is a new field alongside an existing order status (none exists in code) or the order status itself is unsettled.
11	- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider: `docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10` has only Shopper, shop, Payments gateway; `lld/flows.md:3` has only checkout. The change adds two external actors inbound (carriers) and one outbound (email API), a C4 context change for the impact lanes.
12	- Spec says "two shipping carriers" (spec:7) without naming them; C-2 gives the auth model (shared secret per carrier) but not payload formats, signature algorithm, or secret provisioning.
13	- The prompt's addition (guest orders, no account) interacts with spec AC "GET /orders/{id}": a guest has no sign-in, so the read path needs an unguessable link token; the spec's endpoint says nothing about authorisation. The opt-out link (spec:12-13) has the same no-sign-in need.
14	
15	## Features
16	
17	<!-- slice: requirements -->
18	- Run feature: `order-tracking` (C-1; `requirements.md` `## Refined` `feature: order-tracking`). It matches PRD F3 "Order tracking" (`docs/product/prd.md:23`), `features/order-tracking/prd.md`. No correction needed.
19	- Features touched besides it: F2 checkout (creates orders, and the confirmation email the guest link depends on; `prd.md:22`) is a dependency in effect although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` says "Dependencies: None". F4 order management (`prd.md:24`; refund/export, `order-management/prd.md:13-14`) reads the same order resource but is not changed. The living analysis `docs/product/features/order-tracking/analysis/README.md` does not exist (folder holds only `prd.md`), so there is no prior analysis and nothing to reuse.
20	- Candidate contexts (for the synthesis to settle): (1) Shipment status ingestion — carrier webhooks, signature check, per-order history; PRD R3. (2) Order tracking view — `GET /orders/{id}` latest status (and history, R1) incl. guest access by link; PRD R1. (3) Tracking notifications — status-change emails, opt-out per order; PRD R2. Guest access may be its own context or part of (2)/(3), depending on whether a guest token is shared; the impact lanes decide.
21	
22	## Acceptance-criteria review
23	
24	<!-- slice: requirements -->
25	The ticketless spec has four unnumbered criteria (spec:17-21); labelled here S-1..S-4 in order. C-5: they stand as written, so every rewrite is a proposal only.
26	
27	- S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." Ambiguous: "accepted" has no observable failure side (invalid signature, unknown order, unknown status, duplicate or out-of-order delivery), and nothing says the signature is verified though C-2 requires it. Testable only for the happy path.
28	- S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." Ambiguous: "latest" = most recently received or most recent by carrier event time (webhooks can arrive out of order); response shape and the no-updates-yet case unstated; authorisation for guests unstated. Contradicted by code only in that the endpoint and order do not exist.
29	- S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." Ambiguous: a repeated same-status webhook is not a change; whether every one of the five statuses emails (spec:10 says "whenever", PRD R2 "every status change"); who the recipient is for a guest order (the order's email). Delivery failure behaviour unstated.
30	- S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." Testable as written for emails after opt-out; missing: the opt-out link works without sign-in (spec:13) and is in every tracking email, is per order only, and that opt-out does not suppress other orders' emails. Also unclear whether the confirmation email is a "tracking email".
31	- Missing M-1: guest orders (prompt) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email — no spec criterion exists.
32	- Missing M-2: webhook authentication — a status update with an invalid or missing per-carrier signature is rejected and stores nothing (C-2).
33	- Missing M-3: history — every change is kept per order (spec:8; PRD R1 "history"); no criterion states it, and no endpoint shows it.
34	- Missing M-4: only the five statuses of C-3 are accepted; an update naming another status is rejected.
35	- Missing M-5: idempotent/out-of-order handling of repeated webhooks (carriers retry).

---
status: proposed

# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

## Contexts

| Context | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment status ingestion | [shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md) | signed carrier webhooks become validated, per-order status history (PRD R3) |
| Order tracking view | [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md) | `GET /orders/{id}` latest status, guest access by token, the order contract assumed from checkout (PRD R1) |
| Tracking notifications | [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md) | status-change emails, per-order opt-out, confirmation-email guest link (PRD R2) |

## Refined acceptance criteria

The spec's four criteria are unnumbered (spec:17-21), labelled S-1..S-4 in order. Per C-5 they stand as written; every rewrite below is a proposal and is NOT applied to `requirements.md` (state: `proposed — open (C-15)`).

| Criterion | Mark | Proposed rewrite (not applied) | Lands in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." | ambiguous | "A status update with a valid signature for that carrier's secret, naming a known order and one of the five statuses, is accepted (2xx) and appended to that order's history with carrier, status and event time; an invalid or missing signature, unknown order or unknown status is rejected (4xx) and stores nothing." (covers M-2, M-4, M-5) | shipment-status-ingestion |
| S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." | ambiguous | "Returns the latest shipment status (greatest event time) and its event time; an order with no updates returns an explicit 'no shipment status'; a guest order is readable with its link token and without sign-in; a request with neither a valid token nor an authorised account is refused." | order-tracking-view |
| S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." | ambiguous | "When an accepted update changes the latest status, an email naming the new status and the opt-out link goes to the order's email address; an update repeating the current status, or an older one that does not change the latest, sends no email." | tracking-notifications |
| S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." | testable (happy path) | "Following the opt-out link in any tracking email, without signing in, records an opt-out for that order only; no further tracking email is sent for it, while other orders' emails continue." | tracking-notifications |
| M-1 (missing) guest orders | missing | "A guest order (no account) is trackable through the link in its order confirmation email, with no sign-in." | order-tracking-view, tracking-notifications |
| M-3 (missing) history | missing | "Every accepted status update is kept per order and none is overwritten." | shipment-status-ingestion |

M-2 (webhook authentication), M-4 (only the five statuses) and M-5 (duplicates/out-of-order) are folded into the S-1 and S-3 rewrites. Until the user confirms, the spec's wording is the criterion.

## Cross-cutting risks and decisions

Interfaces added (all new; nothing existing changes). Each is designed with `/acs:create-api-contract`:
- Carrier webhook endpoint, signed per carrier ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)).
- `GET /orders/{id}` ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md)).
- Opt-out link endpoint, unauthenticated, per order ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Outbound email-provider HTTP API call and the guest tracking link in the confirmation email ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Persisted shape: per-order status history.

Shared risks and load-bearing surfaces:
- Greenfield dependency: no order model, HTTP layer, persistence, config or checkout exist (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `pyproject.toml:1-6`); the plan must sequence against checkout (C-6). See [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md).
- Unauthenticated, security-sensitive surfaces: webhook signature/secret handling ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)); guest and opt-out token links ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md), [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)). A public API other systems call plus stored shape make this a load-bearing change.
- Out-of-order or duplicate webhooks can regress "latest" and send wrong emails: ingestion decides the rule, notifications consumes it.
- Synchronous email in the webhook path would threaten NFR1 p95 under 300 ms (`docs/product/prd.md:28`); NFR2 90% coverage applies to all new code (`prd.md:29`).
- Docs: C4 context and flows need carriers and the email provider added (owned by ingestion).

## Questions and assumptions

- C-1 answered: feature is `order-tracking`.
- C-2 answered: carriers push signed webhooks, shared secret per carrier, never polled.
- C-3 answered: statuses label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception.
- C-4 answered: transactional email provider unchosen, treated as an outbound HTTP API.
- C-5 answered: spec criteria stand as written; refinements are proposals only.
- C-6 assumed (A-1): tracking assumes an order record (id, customer email, optional account id) from checkout; the minimal contract is listed in [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md). If wrong (this change must create orders), scope grows by an order model and confirmation email.
- C-7 assumed (A-2): one generic payload `{order reference, status, event time}` with a per-carrier HMAC signature header; per-carrier adapters are a seam. If wrong, the intake parsing and signature check change.
- C-8 assumed (B-1): latest = most recent carrier event time, ties by receipt order.
- C-9 assumed (B-2): duplicate same-status webhook stores nothing and sends no email.
- C-10 assumed (B-3): 401 on invalid signature; 4xx on unknown order or status; nothing stored.
- C-11 assumed (B-4): unguessable per-order token is the credential for guest and opt-out links.
- C-12 assumed (B-5): emails sent after the update is stored, not blocking the response; a send failure does not roll back.

1	# /acs:analyze-requirements — revising, reviewing and publishing the draft
2	
3	Open this when a `draft` action carries `findings` (iteration ≥ 2), when the
4	`review` action is due, and when the `publish` action is due. The first
5	draft of a run needs only SKILL.md's Stage 3 and
6	`references/analysis-templates.md`.
7	
8	**Where the cross-references below point.** "Two modes", "Stage 1",
9	"Stage 2" and "Stage 3" are SKILL.md's sections; "The feature" is
10	`references/clarify.md`.
11	
12	## Revising the draft — iteration ≥ 2
13	
14	On iteration ≥ 2 the action's `findings` are the previous iteration's
15	blocking findings, verbatim: put them ALL in the draft pass's `<context>`; it
16	fixes every one and nothing else in the seeded folder (deleting a context file
17	the analysis no longer has), recording them in `iter-<n>/authoring.md`.
18	A reviewer finding that is really a new question for the user — or a draft
19	pass that returns `needs_input` — goes through Stage 2 again (ledger first,
20	then one grouped ask) before the draft pass re-runs with the answers in
21	`<context>`: the controller blocks with `kind: "needs_input"` and hands you
22	`clarify` on the same iteration.
23	
24	The working draft is a folder, `steps/analyze-requirements/iter-<n>/analysis/`
25	— the `draft` action prints it; when an iteration fails, the controller seeds
26	the next iteration's folder with a copy, so the draft is revised in place. The
27	published folder is a copy of those exact bytes (Publishing, below).
28	
29	## The impact review
30	
31	The `review` action. Spawn the three slices it prints (Judge slices, in
32	`references/fan-out.md`) in
33	ONE message, each with `<inputs>` of the draft folder (the action's `draft`,
34	and every file in its `draft_files`, README first), the authoring notes (the
35	action's `notes`), the analyst report (`analyst_report`), `requirements.md`
36	(its `## Refined` section as Stage 2 left it) and, on a ticket run, the ticket
37	file, the clarification ledger, `tech-design.md` when it binds, and the repo paths
38	the impact maps name. Each judges fresh — never forward the
39	analyst's reasoning — and judges EVERY file plus the README's contexts table:
40	the `surface` slice re-derives the impact map from the codebase itself (and
41	whether the contexts split it honestly) and checks that every `## Questions for the user` item was
42	answered in the ledger or carried as an open/assumed entry, and that the
43	confirmed criteria match the refined requirements (and the ticket). Each writes
44	`steps/analyze-requirements/iter-<n>/impact-reviewer-<slice>.md`. Then
45	`record-review`: the controller joins the reports into
46	`iter-<n>/impact-reviewer.md` and derives the verdict from the slices'
47	`<result>` snapshots plus the draft's deterministic checks (below) — never
48	conclude a pass yourself.
49	
50	## The deterministic checks
51	
52	**The deterministic checks run beside the review.** `record-draft` runs the
53	$0 folder checks on the draft as it records it (`acs_lib.analysis_folder`) —
54	the same front-matter specs and section lists the `form` slice re-runs — so
55	they are done before the review spawns, not after it passes; the `review`
56	action lists their findings as `draft_checks`. Per file, they are:
57	
58	```bash
59	# README.md
60	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/front_matter_check.py" \
61	  --require "ticket: str; ready_for_planning: bool" \
62	  --ticket <id> "<draft>/README.md"
63	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/structure_lint.py" \
64	  --sections "Scope and summary; Contexts; Refined acceptance criteria; Cross-cutting risks and decisions; Questions and assumptions; Verdict" \
65	  --ordered "<draft>/README.md"
66	
67	# every context file
68	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/front_matter_check.py" \
69	  --require "context: str" "<draft>/order-checkout.md"
70	python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/structure_lint.py" \
71	  --sections "Impact map; Rules and edge cases; Risks; Open questions; API notes" \
72	  --ordered "<draft>/order-checkout.md"
73	```
74	
75	and, across the folder: every file name is `README.md` or kebab-case `.md`
76	(no `index.md`, no subfolder), every `## Contexts` link resolves to a file in
77	the folder, every context file is linked, and `context` equals its file name.
78	(On a run with no ticket the README spec names `feature: str` in place of
79	`ticket: str` and takes no `--ticket`; a Discovery draft adds the version keys
80	to both specs, and `feature` to the context spec; `record-draft` picks the

# /acs:analyze-requirements — revising, reviewing and publishing the draft

Open this when a `draft` action carries `findings` (iteration ≥ 2), when the
`review` action is due, and when the `publish` action is due. The first
draft of a run needs only SKILL.md's Stage 3 and
`references/analysis-templates.md`.

**Where the cross-references below point.** "Two modes", "Stage 1",
"Stage 2" and "Stage 3" are SKILL.md's sections; "The feature" is
`references/clarify.md`.

## Revising the draft — iteration ≥ 2

On iteration ≥ 2 the action's `findings` are the previous iteration's
blocking findings, verbatim: put them ALL in the draft pass's `<context>`; it
fixes every one and nothing else in the seeded folder (deleting a context file
the analysis no longer has), recording them in `iter-<n>/authoring.md`.
A reviewer finding that is really a new question for the user — or a draft
pass that returns `needs_input` — goes through Stage 2 again (ledger first,
then one grouped ask) before the draft pass re-runs with the answers in
`<context>`: the controller blocks with `kind: "needs_input"` and hands you
`clarify` on the same iteration.

The working draft is a folder, `steps/analyze-requirements/iter-<n>/analysis/`
— the `draft` action prints it; when an iteration fails, the controller seeds
the next iteration's folder with a copy, so the draft is revised in place. The
published folder is a copy of those exact bytes (Publishing, below).

## The impact review

The `review` action. Spawn the three slices it prints (Judge slices, in
`references/fan-out.md`) in
ONE message, each with `<inputs>` of the draft folder (the action's `draft`,
and every file in its `draft_files`, README first), the authoring notes (the
action's `notes`), the analyst report (`analyst_report`), `requirements.md`
(its `## Refined` section as Stage 2 left it) and, on a ticket run, the ticket
file, the clarification ledger, `tech-design.md` when it binds, and the repo paths
the impact maps name. Each judges fresh — never forward the
analyst's reasoning — and judges EVERY file plus the README's contexts table:
the `surface` slice re-derives the impact map from the codebase itself (and
whether the contexts split it honestly) and checks that every `## Questions for the user` item was
answered in the ledger or carried as an open/assumed entry, and that the
confirmed criteria match the refined requirements (and the ticket). Each writes
`steps/analyze-requirements/iter-<n>/impact-reviewer-<slice>.md`. Then
`record-review`: the controller joins the reports into
`iter-<n>/impact-reviewer.md` and derives the verdict from the slices'
`<result>` snapshots plus the draft's deterministic checks (below) — never
conclude a pass yourself.

## The deterministic checks

**The deterministic checks run beside the review.** `record-draft` runs the
$0 folder checks on the draft as it records it (`acs_lib.analysis_folder`) —
the same front-matter specs and section lists the `form` slice re-runs — so
they are done before the review spawns, not after it passes; the `review`
action lists their findings as `draft_checks`. Per file, they are:

```bash
# README.md
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/front_matter_check.py" \
  --require "ticket: str; ready_for_planning: bool" \
  --ticket <id> "<draft>/README.md"
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/structure_lint.py" \
  --sections "Scope and summary; Contexts; Refined acceptance criteria; Cross-cutting risks and decisions; Questions and assumptions; Verdict" \
  --ordered "<draft>/README.md"

# every context file
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/front_matter_check.py" \
  --require "context: str" "<draft>/order-checkout.md"
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/structure_lint.py" \
  --sections "Impact map; Rules and edge cases; Risks; Open questions; API notes" \
  --ordered "<draft>/order-checkout.md"
```

and, across the folder: every file name is `README.md` or kebab-case `.md`
(no `index.md`, no subfolder), every `## Contexts` link resolves to a file in
the folder, every context file is linked, and `context` equals its file name.
(On a run with no ticket the README spec names `feature: str` in place of
`ticket: str` and takes no `--ticket`; a Discovery draft adds the version keys
to both specs, and `feature` to the context spec; `record-draft` picks the
specs from the run — you never choose them.)

`record-review` folds them into that iteration's blocking findings: a check
finding fails the iteration like a judge's blocking finding (it goes to the
next draft pass, or ends the run at the cap), never patched by you.

## Publishing

Once those pass, `publish` copies
every file of the draft folder byte-for-byte to the resolved analysis folder —
the feature's living analysis on a Discovery run,
`<development_dir>/<feature>/<ticket-id or run-id>/analysis/` on a shared
Development run, the run's state folder on a LOCAL one (recorded in
`publication`, never in `publication.files`) — removes a context file the new
analysis no longer has (only inside that folder), reads every file back, and
records the repo paths it wrote as `publication.files` in the loop,
repo-relative, with each file's sha. It never
stages, commits or pushes and refuses no branch (ADR-0127): the files are left
as uncommitted changes in the working tree, and `/acs:create-pr` reads those
recorded paths to make the documents commit, the first of the PR.
`record-publication` re-derives it from the working tree — every published
file is still the reviewed bytes — and completes the loop.

You never copy or commit the analysis yourself, and no subagent does: the
file-map write guard (`acs_lib/filemap.py`) denies any running `write`-kind
agent — the analyst included — a write under the run's document folders, because
these documents are precisely the control inputs an implementer is checked
against. The partition draft is workspace state and is never committed.

The front-matter check uses the same parser the gates and the analysis
folder check use, so a draft it accepts cannot be rejected downstream for its
front matter.

**The published file is the reusable record.** The run's
analysis folder is what `/acs:create-impl-plan`, `/acs:create-api-contract` and
`/acs:create-test-docs` read, and what the next run of this skill starts from
(Stage 1's reuse); the feature's living analysis is what the Design skills
(`/acs:create-architecture`, `/acs:create-data-design`, `/acs:create-flows`,
`/acs:create-tech-design`) read and what every later Development run on the feature
starts from. Every reader opens the README first (`artifacts["analysis.md"]`)
and then only the context files it needs (`analysis_files`). The partition
copy exists only for the no-checkout case, where there is no docs folder to
publish to.

# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

## Contexts

| Context | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment status ingestion | [shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md) | signed carrier webhooks become validated, per-order status history (PRD R3) |
| Order tracking view | [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md) | `GET /orders/{id}` latest status, guest access by token, the order contract assumed from checkout (PRD R1) |
| Tracking notifications | [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md) | status-change emails, per-order opt-out, confirmation-email guest link (PRD R2) |

## Refined acceptance criteria

The spec's four criteria are unnumbered (spec:17-21), labelled S-1..S-4 in order. Per C-5 they stand as written; every rewrite below is a proposal and is NOT applied to `requirements.md` (state: `proposed — open (C-15)`).

## Cross-cutting risks and decisions

Interfaces added (all new; nothing existing changes). Each is designed with `/acs:create-api-contract`:
- Carrier webhook endpoint, signed per carrier ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)).
- `GET /orders/{id}` ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md)).
- Opt-out link endpoint, unauthenticated, per order ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Outbound email-provider HTTP API call and the guest tracking link in the confirmation email ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Persisted shape: per-order status history.

Shared risks and load-bearing surfaces:
- Greenfield dependency: no order model, HTTP layer, persistence, config or checkout exist (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `pyproject.toml:1-6`); the plan must sequence against checkout (C-6). See [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md).
- Unauthenticated, security-sensitive surfaces: webhook signature/secret handling ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)); guest and opt-out token links ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md), [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)). A public API other systems call plus stored shape make this a load-bearing change.
- Out-of-order or duplicate webhooks can regress "latest" and send wrong emails: ingestion decides the rule, notifications consumes it.
- Synchronous email in the webhook path would threaten NFR1 p95 under 300 ms (`docs/product/prd.md:28`); NFR2 90% coverage applies to all new code (`prd.md:29`).
- Docs: C4 context and flows need carriers and the email provider added (owned by ingestion).

## Questions and assumptions

- C-1 answered: feature is `order-tracking`.
- C-2 answered: carriers push signed webhooks, shared secret per carrier, never polled.
- C-3 answered: statuses label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception.
- C-4 answered: transactional email provider unchosen, treated as an outbound HTTP API.
- C-5 answered: spec criteria stand as written; refinements are proposals only.
- C-6 assumed (A-1): tracking assumes an order record (id, customer email, optional account id) from checkout; the minimal contract is listed in [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md). If wrong (this change must create orders), scope grows by an order model and confirmation email.
- C-7 assumed (A-2): one generic payload `{order reference, status, event time}` with a per-carrier HMAC signature header; per-carrier adapters are a seam. If wrong, the intake parsing and signature check change.
- C-8 assumed (B-1): latest = most recent carrier event time, ties by receipt order.
- C-9 assumed (B-2): duplicate same-status webhook stores nothing and sends no email.
- C-10 assumed (B-3): 401 on invalid signature; 4xx on unknown order or status; nothing stored.
- C-11 assumed (B-4): unguessable per-order token is the credential for guest and opt-out links.
- C-12 assumed (B-5): emails sent after the update is stored, not blocking the response; a send failure does not roll back.
- C-13 assumed (B-6): opt-out covers that order's status-change emails only, not the confirmation email, not reversible here.
- C-14 assumed (B-7): `GET /orders/{id}` exposes latest status only; history stored, exposed later (PRD R1 "history" left open).
- C-15 assumed: the S-1..S-4, M-1, M-3 rewrites stay proposals, unapplied (user unreachable; consistent with C-5).

Assumptions C-6..C-15 were taken because the user was unreachable; each is a default the user can still correct.

## Verdict

`ready_for_planning: true`. The only open questions, A-1 (C-6) and A-2 (C-7), have stated proceed-on defaults and neither makes every default build the wrong thing: A-1 changes plan sequencing against checkout, A-2 is isolated behind a per-carrier adapter seam. The B-defaults are conventional. The plan must treat C-6 and C-7 as assumptions and sequence order creation (checkout) before or alongside this work.

# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

# Order tracking — product spec (draft from product)

Shoppers want to know where their order is without emailing support.

## What we want

1. Our two shipping carriers push shipment status changes to us; we keep
   every change per order.
2. `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest shipment status of the order.
3. The shopper gets an email whenever the shipment status of their order
   changes.
4. A shopper can opt out of tracking emails for one order, from a link in any
   tracking email, without signing in.

- Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order.
- GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order.
- The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes.
- A shopper who opted out of an order's tracking emails gets no further ones

# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

## Contexts

| Context | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment status ingestion | [shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md) | signed carrier webhooks become validated, per-order status history (PRD R3) |
| Order tracking view | [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md) | `GET /orders/{id}` latest status, guest access by token, the order contract assumed from checkout (PRD R1) |
| Tracking notifications | [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md) | status-change emails, per-order opt-out, confirmation-email guest link (PRD R2) |

## Refined acceptance criteria

The spec's four criteria are unnumbered (spec:17-21), labelled S-1..S-4 in order. Per C-5 they stand as written; every rewrite below is a proposal and is NOT applied to `requirements.md` (state: `proposed — open (C-15)`).

| Criterion | Mark | Proposed rewrite (not applied) | Lands in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." | ambiguous | "A status update with a valid signature for that carrier's secret, naming a known order and one of the five statuses, is accepted (2xx) and appended to that order's history with carrier, status and event time; an invalid or missing signature, unknown order or unknown status is rejected (4xx) and stores nothing." (covers M-2, M-4, M-5) | shipment-status-ingestion |
| S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." | ambiguous | "Returns the latest shipment status (greatest event time) and its event time; an order with no updates returns an explicit 'no shipment status'; a guest order is readable with its link token and without sign-in; a request with neither a valid token nor an authorised account is refused." | order-tracking-view |
| S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." | ambiguous | "When an accepted update changes the latest status, an email naming the new status and the opt-out link goes to the order's email address; an update repeating the current status, or an older one that does not change the latest, sends no email." | tracking-notifications |
| S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." | testable (happy path) | "Following the opt-out link in any tracking email, without signing in, records an opt-out for that order only; no further tracking email is sent for it, while other orders' emails continue." | tracking-notifications |
| M-1 (missing) guest orders | missing | "A guest order (no account) is trackable through the link in its order confirmation email, with no sign-in." | order-tracking-view, tracking-notifications |
| M-3 (missing) history | missing | "Every accepted status update is kept per order and none is overwritten." | shipment-status-ingestion |

M-2 (webhook authentication), M-4 (only the five statuses) and M-5 (duplicates/out-of-order) are folded into the S-1 and S-3 rewrites. Until the user confirms, the spec's wording is the criterion.

## Cross-cutting risks and decisions

Interfaces added (all new; nothing existing changes). Each is designed with `/acs:create-api-contract`:
- Carrier webhook endpoint, signed per carrier ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)).
- `GET /orders/{id}` ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md)).
- Opt-out link endpoint, unauthenticated, per order ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Outbound email-provider HTTP API call and the guest tracking link in the confirmation email ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Persisted shape: per-order status history.

Shared risks and load-bearing surfaces:
- Greenfield dependency: no order model, HTTP layer, persistence, config or checkout exist (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `pyproject.toml:1-6`); the plan must sequence against checkout (C-6). See [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md).
- Unauthenticated, security-sensitive surfaces: webhook signature/secret handling ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)); guest and opt-out token links ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md), [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)). ## Problem and disagreements

<!-- slice: requirements -->
The requirements (`requirements.md`, prompt; spec `attachments/order-tracking-spec.md`:1-21; ledger C-1..C-5) ask for: carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2), every change stored per order (spec:7-8); `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9); an email on every status change via an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4); per-order opt-out from a link in any tracking email, no sign-in (spec:12-13); plus guest orders trackable via the link in their order confirmation email (prompt). Statuses: label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception (C-3).

Disagreements and gaps against the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept at all. `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`; there is no HTTP framework, no persistence, no `/orders` route. "GET /orders/{id} shows the latest status" (spec:9) therefore describes a new endpoint on an order resource that does not exist yet; checkout (F2, `docs/product/prd.md:22`, roadmap Q4 `docs/product/roadmap.md:3`) is what would create orders and is not built. Order tracking is roadmap Q1 (`roadmap.md:4`), after checkout.
- The "order confirmation email" the guest addition relies on is not in any PRD feature: checkout R1/R2 (`features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`) mention no confirmation email, and order-tracking R2 covers status-change emails only (`features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`). No guest/account model exists in PRD or code; the PRD personas only list Shopper and Merchant (`prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD order-tracking R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); spec item 2 and its AC expose only the latest status. History is stored (spec:8) but no criterion exposes it.
- PRD R3 "carrier updates move an order's status" (`order-tracking/prd.md:15`) vs. the spec's separate shipment status: the spec calls it "shipment status" (spec:9,10,18), the PRD "an order's status". Whether shipment status is a new field alongside an existing order status (none exists in code) or the order status itself is unsettled.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider: `docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10` has only Shopper, shop, Payments gateway; `lld/flows.md:3` has only checkout. The change adds two external actors inbound (carriers) and one outbound (email API), a C4 context change for the impact lanes.
- Spec says "two shipping carriers" (spec:7) without naming them; C-2 gives the auth model (shared secret per carrier) but not payload formats, signature algorithm, or secret provisioning.
- The prompt's addition (guest orders, no account) interacts with spec AC "GET /orders/{id}": a guest has no sign-in, so the read path needs an unguessable link token; the spec's endpoint says nothing about authorisation. The opt-out link (spec:12-13) has the same no-sign-in need.

- Features touched besides it: F2 checkout (creates orders, and the confirmation email the guest link depends on; `prd.md:22`) is a dependency in effect although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` says "Dependencies: None". - Candidate contexts (for the synthesis to settle): (1) Shipment status ingestion — carrier webhooks, signature check, per-order history; PRD R3. (2) Order tracking view — `GET /orders/{id}` latest status (and history, R1) incl. guest access by link; PRD R1. (3) Tracking notifications — status-change emails, opt-out per order; PRD R2. Guest access may be its own context or part of (2)/(3), depending on whether a guest token is shared; the impact lanes decide.

## Acceptance-criteria review

<!-- slice: requirements -->
The ticketless spec has four unnumbered criteria (spec:17-21); labelled here S-1..S-4 in order. C-5: they stand as written, so every rewrite is a proposal only.

- S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." Ambiguous: "accepted" has no observable failure side (invalid signature, unknown order, unknown status, duplicate or out-of-order delivery), and nothing says the signature is verified though C-2 requires it. Testable only for the happy path.
- S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." Ambiguous: "latest" = most recently received or most recent by carrier event time (webhooks can arrive out of order); response shape and the no-updates-yet case unstated; authorisation for guests unstated. Contradicted by code only in that the endpoint and order do not exist.
- S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." Ambiguous: a repeated same-status webhook is not a change; whether every one of the five statuses emails (spec:10 says "whenever", PRD R2 "every status change"); who the recipient is for a guest order (the order's email). Delivery failure behaviour unstated.
- S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." Testable as written for emails after opt-out; missing: the opt-out link works without sign-in (spec:13) and is in every tracking email, is per order only, and that opt-out does not suppress other orders' emails. Also unclear whether the confirmation email is a "tracking email".
- Missing M-1: guest orders (prompt) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email — no spec criterion exists.
- Missing M-2: webhook authentication — a status update with an invalid or missing per-carrier signature is rejected and stores nothing (C-2).
- Missing M-3: history — every change is kept per order (spec:8; PRD R1 "history"); no criterion states it, and no endpoint shows it.
- Missing M-4: only the five statuses of C-3 are accepted; an update naming another status is rejected.
- Missing M-5: idempotent/out-of-order handling of repeated webhooks (carriers retry).

Rewrites are in group (c).

## Risks

<!-- slice: requirements -->
- Hard dependency on unbuilt functionality: no order model, no HTTP layer, no checkout, no confirmation email (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `README.md:5-8`, roadmap `roadmap.md:3-4`). The analysis must say what this change creates versus assumes; delivering tracking before checkout means tracking has no orders to track. Evidence: above.
- Security of the unauthenticated surfaces: webhook endpoint (signature, replay) and guest link/opt-out link (token guessability, enumeration of `GET /orders/{id}` by sequential id). Evidence: C-2, spec:12-13, prompt addition.
- Webhook out-of-order/duplicate delivery can regress "latest" status (e.g. delivered then in_transit) and send wrong emails (spec:9-10).
- Email provider unchosen (C-4): vendor lock-in is avoided by treating it as an outbound HTTP API, but delivery failures, retries and rate limits are unspecified; emailing synchronously within the webhook request threatens NFR1 p95 under 300 ms (`prd.md:28`).
- Privacy: emailing shoppers and the guest address handling; opt-out is legally relevant for marketing mail but tracking mail is transactional — wording of the opt-out criterion matters. No PRD statement on retention.
- NFR2 coverage 90% (`prd.md:29`) applies to all new code.
- Scope fork: PRD order-tracking R1 "history" vs. spec "latest" (see disagreements).

<!-- slice: repo -->
- Greenfield: no web framework, routing, persistence, order model, config or dependency exists (src/shop/__init__.py:1-9, pyproject.toml:1-6). The planner must choose or find these elsewhere; this is not a small attach.
- Security-sensitive paths, new: webhook signature verification with a per-carrier secret (secret storage/config has no home yet); unauthenticated opt-out and guest-tracking links need unguessable per-order tokens (spec :12-13). Load-bearing surfaces: the webhook intake and the token links.
- Webhook semantics: duplicate/out-of-order deliveries affect "latest status" vs history (spec :7-9); no ordering rule in the sources.
- Email provider unchosen and outbound call can fail; sending in the webhook request path couples carrier ack to provider availability (answer 3).
- Dependency: guest and registered order data and a confirmation email do not exist in code; PRD for checkout is placeholder text (checkout PRD :13-14).
- Test suite is tiny and fast; no flaky suites observed.

# Order tracking view

## Impact map

| Path | Component | Change | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/shop/__init__.py` | shop package root (`health`, `list_customers`, `PAGE_SIZE`) | possible export/wiring point only; no routing or order model to extend | `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`; `pyproject.toml` pythonpath `src` |
| `src/shop/` `GET /orders/{id}` handler (new) | order read exposing latest shipment status | new endpoint; guest access by token | spec `attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:9,18`; no `orders` in code (grep) |
| `tests/test_order_tracking_view.py` (new) | read-path tests | new: latest status, no-update case, guest token, refusal | `tests/test_health.py:1-6` convention |
| `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md` | feature PRD (R1 status+history, R2, R3) | possible refinement note: guest tracking and per-order opt-out absent; F2 dependency undeclared | `prd.md:13-15,21-23` |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `pyproject.toml` | release notes, version 2.4.0 | likely changelog entry; HTTP framework choice touches dependencies (none declared) | `CHANGELOG.md:1-5`; `pyproject.toml:1-3` |

## Rules and edge cases

- Returns latest shipment status only (spec:9; C-14); history is stored by [shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md) but not exposed. PRD R1 "history" stays open.
