# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

## Contexts

| Context | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment status ingestion | [shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md) | signed carrier webhooks become validated, per-order status history (PRD R3) |
| Order tracking view | [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md) | `GET /orders/{id}` latest status, guest access by token, the order contract assumed from checkout (PRD R1) |
| Tracking notifications | [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md) | status-change emails, per-order opt-out, confirmation-email guest link (PRD R2) |

## Refined acceptance criteria

The spec's four criteria are unnumbered (spec:17-21), labelled S-1..S-4 in order. Per C-5 they stand as written; every rewrite below is a proposal and is NOT applied to `requirements.md` (state: `proposed — open (C-15)`).

| Criterion | Mark | Proposed rewrite (not applied) | Lands in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." | ambiguous | "A status update with a valid signature for that carrier's secret, naming a known order and one of the five statuses, is accepted (2xx) and appended to that order's history with carrier, status and event time; an invalid or missing signature, unknown order or unknown status is rejected (4xx) and stores nothing." (covers M-2, M-4, M-5) | shipment-status-ingestion |
| S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." | ambiguous | "Returns the latest shipment status (greatest event time) and its event time; an order with no updates returns an explicit 'no shipment status'; a guest order is readable with its link token and without sign-in; a request with neither a valid token nor an authorised account is refused." | order-tracking-view |
| S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." | ambiguous | "When an accepted update changes the latest status, an email naming the new status and the opt-out link goes to the order's email address; an update repeating the current status, or an older one that does not change the latest, sends no email." | tracking-notifications |
| S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." | testable (happy path) | "Following the opt-out link in any tracking email, without signing in, records an opt-out for that order only; no further tracking email is sent for it, while other orders' emails continue." | tracking-notifications |
| M-1 (missing) guest orders | missing | "A guest order (no account) is trackable through the link in its order confirmation email, with no sign-in." | order-tracking-view, tracking-notifications |
| M-3 (missing) history | missing | "Every accepted status update is kept per order and none is overwritten." | shipment-status-ingestion |

M-2 (webhook authentication), M-4 (only the five statuses) and M-5 (duplicates/out-of-order) are folded into the S-1 and S-3 rewrites. Until the user confirms, the spec's wording is the criterion.

## Cross-cutting risks and decisions

Interfaces added (all new; nothing existing changes). Each is designed with `/acs:create-api-contract`:
- Carrier webhook endpoint, signed per carrier ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)).
- `GET /orders/{id}` ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md)).
- Opt-out link endpoint, unauthenticated, per order ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Outbound email-provider HTTP API call and the guest tracking link in the confirmation email ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Persisted shape: per-order status history.

Shared risks and load-bearing surfaces:
- Greenfield dependency: no order model, HTTP layer, persistence, config or checkout exist (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `pyproject.toml:1-6`); the plan must sequence against checkout (C-6). See [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md).
- Unauthenticated, security-sensitive surfaces: webhook signature/secret handling ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)); guest and opt-out token links ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md), [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)). A public API other systems call plus stored shape make this a load-bearing change.
- Out-of-order or duplicate webhooks can regress "latest" and send wrong emails: ingestion decides the rule, notifications consumes it.
- Synchronous email in the webhook path would threaten NFR1 p95 under 300 ms (`docs/product/prd.md:28`); NFR2 90% coverage applies to all new code (`prd.md:29`).
- Docs: C4 context and flows need carriers and the email provider added (owned by ingestion).

## Questions and assumptions

- C-1 answered: feature is `order-tracking`.
- C-2 answered: carriers push signed webhooks, shared secret per carrier, never polled.
- C-3 answered: statuses label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception.
- C-4 answered: transactional email provider unchosen, treated as an outbound HTTP API.
- C-5 answered: spec criteria stand as written; refinements are proposals only.
- C-6 assumed (A-1): tracking assumes an order record (id, customer email, optional account id) from checkout; the minimal contract is listed in [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md). If wrong (this change must create orders), scope grows by an order model and confirmation email.
- C-7 assumed (A-2): one generic payload `{order reference, status, event time}` with a per-carrier HMAC signature header; per-carrier adapters are a seam. If wrong, the intake parsing and signature check change.
- C-8 assumed (B-1): latest = most recent carrier event time, ties by receipt order.
- C-9 assumed (B-2): duplicate same-status webhook stores nothing and sends no email.
- C-10 assumed (B-3): 401 on invalid signature; 4xx on unknown order or status; nothing stored.
- C-11 assumed (B-4): unguessable per-order token is the credential for guest and opt-out links.
- C-12 assumed (B-5): emails sent after the update is stored, not blocking the response; a send failure does not roll back.
- C-13 assumed (B-6): opt-out covers that order's status-change emails only, not the confirmation email, not reversible here.
- C-14 assumed (B-7): `GET /orders/{id}` exposes latest status only; history stored, exposed later (PRD R1 "history" left open).
- C-15 assumed: the S-1..S-4, M-1, M-3 rewrites stay proposals, unapplied (user unreachable; consistent with C-5).

Assumptions C-6..C-15 were taken because the user was unreachable; each is a default the user can still correct.

## Verdict

`ready_for_planning: true`. The only open questions, A-1 (C-6) and A-2 (C-7), have stated proceed-on defaults and neither makes every default build the wrong thing: A-1 changes plan sequencing against checkout, A-2 is isolated behind a per-carrier adapter seam. The B-defaults are conventional. The plan must treat C-6 and C-7 as assumptions and sequence order creation (checkout) before or alongside this work.

## Rules and edge cases

- Carriers push, never polled; one shared secret per carrier (C-2). Reject an invalid or missing signature with 401, store nothing (C-10, assumed).
- Only `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` are accepted (C-3); another status, or an unknown order, is a 4xx and stores nothing (C-10).

## Risks

- Load-bearing: unauthenticated public webhook endpoint and per-carrier secret storage (`src/shop/tracking/`); there is no config or secret home in the repo (`pyproject.toml:1-6`). Consider constant-time signature comparison and replay handling; stored history is a new persisted shape with no persistence layer to build on.
- Out-of-order and retried deliveries (spec:7-9; no ordering rule in the sources).
- Webhook ack must not wait on email (C-12; NFR1, `docs/product/prd.md:28`).
- Unconfirmed payload contract (C-7) may force rework; keep per-carrier adapters behind one interface.

## Open questions

- C-7 assumed: carrier payload, signature algorithm, order matching.
- C-8, C-9, C-10 assumed (conventional defaults).

## API notes

New inbound carrier webhook endpoint, one signed route or header scheme per carrier (C-2, C-7); responses 2xx/401/4xx per C-10. Persisted: per-order status history. Design with `/acs:create-api-contract`.

- The confirmation email and guest identity are unbuilt (C-6).

- C-4 answered; C-6, C-12, C-13 assumed.

# Order tracking — product spec (draft from product)

Shoppers want to know where their order is without emailing support.

## What we want

1. Our two shipping carriers push shipment status changes to us; we keep
   every change per order.
2. `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest shipment status of the order.
3. The shopper gets an email whenever the shipment status of their order
   changes.
4. A shopper can opt out of tracking emails for one order, from a link in any
   tracking email, without signing in.

## Acceptance criteria

- Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order.
- GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order.
- The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes.
- A shopper who opted out of an order's tracking emails gets no further ones
  for that order.

# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

`review` action is due, and when the `publish` action is due. The first

**Where the cross-references below point.** "Two modes", "Stage 1",
"Stage 2" and "Stage 3" are SKILL.md's sections; "The feature" is
`references/clarify.md`.

## Revising the draft — iteration ≥ 2

On iteration ≥ 2 the action's `findings` are the previous iteration's
blocking findings, verbatim: put them ALL in the draft pass's `<context>`; it
fixes every one and nothing else in the seeded folder (deleting a context file
the analysis no longer has), recording them in `iter-<n>/authoring.md`.
A reviewer finding that is really a new question for the user — or a draft
pass that returns `needs_input` — goes through Stage 2 again (ledger first,
then one grouped ask) before the draft pass re-runs with the answers in
`<context>`: the controller blocks with `kind: "needs_input"` and hands you
`clarify` on the same iteration.

The working draft is a folder, `steps/analyze-requirements/iter-<n>/analysis/`
— the `draft` action prints it; when an iteration fails, the controller seeds
the next iteration's folder with a copy, so the draft is revised in place. The
published folder is a copy of those exact bytes (Publishing, below).

## The impact review

The `review` action. Spawn the three slices it prints (Judge slices, in
`references/fan-out.md`) in
ONE message, each with `<inputs>` of the draft folder (the action's `draft`,
and every file in its `draft_files`, README first), the authoring notes (the
action's `notes`), the analyst report (`analyst_report`), `requirements.md`
(its `## Refined` section as Stage 2 left it) and, on a ticket run, the ticket
file, the clarification ledger, `tech-design.md` when it binds, and the repo paths
the impact maps name. Each judges fresh — never forward the
analyst's reasoning — and judges EVERY file plus the README's contexts table:
the `surface` slice re-derives the impact map from the codebase itself (and
whether the contexts split it honestly) and checks that every `## Questions for the user` item was
answered in the ledger or carried as an open/assumed entry, and that the
confirmed criteria match the refined requirements (and the ticket). Each writes
`steps/analyze-requirements/iter-<n>/impact-reviewer-<slice>.md`. Then
`record-review`: the controller joins the reports into
`iter-<n>/impact-reviewer.md` and derives the verdict from the slices'
`<result>` snapshots plus the draft's deterministic checks (below) — never
conclude a pass yourself.

# Analysis — order-tracking: carrier-driven shipment status, tracking view and emails

## Scope and summary

Carriers push signed webhook status changes (shared secret per carrier, never polled; C-2). Every change is stored per order (`attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8`), `GET /orders/{id}` shows the latest status (spec:9), the shopper is emailed on every change through an outbound HTTP email API (spec:10-11, C-4), and can opt out per order from a link in any tracking email without signing in (spec:12-13). The user's addition: guest orders (no account) are trackable through the link in their order confirmation email. Statuses: `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` (C-3). Out of scope: polling carriers, choosing the email provider, building checkout.

Disagreements with the code and docs:
- The repo has no order concept, HTTP layer or persistence: `src/shop/__init__.py:1-9` holds only `PAGE_SIZE`, `health()` and a stub `list_customers`; `README.md:5-8` documents only `GET /health` and `GET /customers`. `GET /orders/{id}` is a new endpoint on a resource that does not exist; this is greenfield, not a small attach.
- The confirmation email the guest link relies on is in no PRD feature (`docs/product/features/checkout-with-card-payments/prd.md:13-14`, `docs/product/features/order-tracking/prd.md:14`), and no guest/account model exists (`docs/product/prd.md:9-10`).
- PRD R1 promises "status and history" (`order-tracking/prd.md:13`); the spec exposes only the latest status.
- The architecture set knows no carrier or email provider (`docs/architecture/hld/c4-context.md:3-10`, `lld/flows.md:3`).
- Checkout (F2) is a de-facto dependency although `order-tracking/prd.md:21-23` lists none; roadmap puts checkout before tracking (`docs/product/roadmap.md:3-4`). No living analysis for this feature exists, so nothing was reused.

## Contexts

| Context | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment status ingestion | [shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md) | signed carrier webhooks become validated, per-order status history (PRD R3) |
| Order tracking view | [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md) | `GET /orders/{id}` latest status, guest access by token, the order contract assumed from checkout (PRD R1) |
| Tracking notifications | [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md) | status-change emails, per-order opt-out, confirmation-email guest link (PRD R2) |

## Refined acceptance criteria

The spec's four criteria are unnumbered (spec:17-21), labelled S-1..S-4 in order. Per C-5 they stand as written; every rewrite below is a proposal and is NOT applied to `requirements.md` (state: `proposed — open (C-15)`).

| Criterion | Mark | Proposed rewrite (not applied) | Lands in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S-1 "Carrier status updates are accepted and stored per order." | ambiguous | "A status update with a valid signature for that carrier's secret, naming a known order and one of the five statuses, is accepted (2xx) and appended to that order's history with carrier, status and event time; an invalid or missing signature, unknown order or unknown status is rejected (4xx) and stores nothing." (covers M-2, M-4, M-5) | shipment-status-ingestion |
| S-2 "GET /orders/{id} returns the latest shipment status of the order." | ambiguous | "Returns the latest shipment status (greatest event time) and its event time; an order with no updates returns an explicit 'no shipment status'; a guest order is readable with its link token and without sign-in; a request with neither a valid token nor an authorised account is refused." | order-tracking-view |
| S-3 "The shopper is emailed when the shipment status of their order changes." | ambiguous | "When an accepted update changes the latest status, an email naming the new status and the opt-out link goes to the order's email address; an update repeating the current status, or an older one that does not change the latest, sends no email." | tracking-notifications |
| S-4 "A shopper who opted out ... gets no further ones for that order." | testable (happy path) | "Following the opt-out link in any tracking email, without signing in, records an opt-out for that order only; no further tracking email is sent for it, while other orders' emails continue." | tracking-notifications |
| M-1 (missing) guest orders | missing | "A guest order (no account) is trackable through the link in its order confirmation email, with no sign-in." | order-tracking-view, tracking-notifications |
| M-3 (missing) history | missing | "Every accepted status update is kept per order and none is overwritten." | shipment-status-ingestion |

M-2 (webhook authentication), M-4 (only the five statuses) and M-5 (duplicates/out-of-order) are folded into the S-1 and S-3 rewrites. Until the user confirms, the spec's wording is the criterion.

## Cross-cutting risks and decisions

Interfaces added (all new; nothing existing changes). Each is designed with `/acs:create-api-contract`:
- Carrier webhook endpoint, signed per carrier ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)).
- `GET /orders/{id}` ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md)).
- Opt-out link endpoint, unauthenticated, per order ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Outbound email-provider HTTP API call and the guest tracking link in the confirmation email ([tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)).
- Persisted shape: per-order status history.

Shared risks and load-bearing surfaces:
- Greenfield dependency: no order model, HTTP layer, persistence, config or checkout exist (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`, `pyproject.toml:1-6`); the plan must sequence against checkout (C-6). See [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md).
- Unauthenticated, security-sensitive surfaces: webhook signature/secret handling ([shipment-status-ingestion.md](shipment-status-ingestion.md)); guest and opt-out token links ([order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md), [tracking-notifications.md](tracking-notifications.md)). A public API other systems call plus stored shape make this a load-bearing change.
- Out-of-order or duplicate webhooks can regress "latest" and send wrong emails: ingestion decides the rule, notifications consumes it.
- Synchronous email in the webhook path would threaten NFR1 p95 under 300 ms (`docs/product/prd.md:28`); NFR2 90% coverage applies to all new code (`prd.md:29`).
- Docs: C4 context and flows need carriers and the email provider added (owned by ingestion).

## Questions and assumptions

- C-1 answered: feature is `order-tracking`.
- C-2 answered: carriers push signed webhooks, shared secret per carrier, never polled.
- C-3 answered: statuses label_created, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception.
- C-4 answered: transactional email provider unchosen, treated as an outbound HTTP API.
- C-5 answered: spec criteria stand as written; refinements are proposals only.
- C-6 assumed (A-1): tracking assumes an order record (id, customer email, optional account id) from checkout; the minimal contract is listed in [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md). If wrong (this change must create orders), scope grows by an order model and confirmation email.
- C-7 assumed (A-2): one generic payload `{order reference, status, event time}` with a per-carrier HMAC signature header; per-carrier adapters are a seam. If wrong, the intake parsing and signature check change.
- C-8 assumed (B-1): latest = most recent carrier event time, ties by receipt order.
- C-9 assumed (B-2): duplicate same-status webhook stores nothing and sends no email.
- C-10 assumed (B-3): 401 on invalid signature; 4xx on unknown order or status; nothing stored.
- C-11 assumed (B-4): unguessable per-order token is the credential for guest and opt-out links.
- C-12 assumed (B-5): emails sent after the update is stored, not blocking the response; a send failure does not roll back.
- C-13 assumed (B-6): opt-out covers that order's status-change emails only, not the confirmation email, not reversible here.
- C-14 assumed (B-7): `GET /orders/{id}` exposes latest status only; history stored, exposed later (PRD R1 "history" left open).
- C-15 assumed: the S-1..S-4, M-1, M-3 rewrites stay proposals, unapplied (user unreachable; consistent with C-5).

Assumptions C-6..C-15 were taken because the user was unreachable; each is a default the user can still correct.

## Verdict

`ready_for_planning: true`. The only open questions, A-1 (C-6) and A-2 (C-7), have stated proceed-on defaults and neither makes every default build the wrong thing: A-1 changes plan sequencing against checkout, A-2 is isolated behind a per-carrier adapter seam. The B-defaults are conventional. The plan must treat C-6 and C-7 as assumptions and sequence order creation (checkout) before or alongside this work.

| `src/shop/tracking/` (new; modules are the planner's call) | carrier webhook intake, signature check, status history store | new: per-carrier signed intake, validation against the five statuses, append-only history | spec `attachments/order-tracking-spec.md:7-8,17`; package `shop` under `src` (`pyproject.toml:1-6`); nothing like it exists (`src/shop/__init__.py:1-9`) |

The `README.md` `## API` row for the webhook endpoint is owned by [order-tracking-view.md](order-tracking-view.md).

## Rules and edge cases

- Carriers push, never polled; one shared secret per carrier (C-2). Reject an invalid or missing signature with 401, store nothing (C-10, assumed).
- Only `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `exception` are accepted (C-3); another status, or an unknown order, is a 4xx and stores nothing (C-10).
- Every accepted change is kept in history per order (spec:8); duplicates of the current status store nothing new (C-9).
- Latest = greatest carrier event time, ties by receipt order (C-8). Test: `delivered` then a late `in_transit` must not regress latest.

# /acs:analyze-requirements — the result document and the report

Read this at Finish: before you write `steps/analyze-requirements/result.json`
(the example is SKILL.md's), what each canonical `states` key means and
must equal, and what a failed run keeps; before you report a direct
invocation, what its summary covers.

## The `states` keys

Canonical `states` keys — EXACT names; `acs step finish` documents
them and the next steps read them:
- `ready_for_planning` (bool): the verdict. `false` is the `needs_input`
  arm, and `/acs:create-impl-plan` is what consumes it. It MUST equal the
  published front matter's `ready_for_planning` (the README's) — a result
  document that disagrees with it is a defect, not a second opinion. There is
  no `api_surface` key any more (ADR-0134): an interface change is named in
  the README and pointed to `/acs:create-api-contract`.
- `questions_open` (int): clarifications still unanswered in the ledger —
  the count `clarify.py list --open` (`--ticket <id>` on a ticket run)
  prints after this run.
- `files` (array): every repo-relative path this run wrote and left
  uncommitted — the publish action's `publication.files` (every file of
  the published analysis folder, README first: the feature's living
  analysis on a Discovery run, e.g.
  `docs/product/features/wishlist/analysis/README.md`). `/acs:create-pr` commits
  them; empty when nothing was published or the analysis was kept local.

Confirmed criteria and features are applied through their own CLI
(`acs.py requirements refine`), so they belong in
`findings` and the completion report, not in `states`. On failure keep
whatever is true: `ready_for_planning: false`, the open findings in
`findings`, and the reason (`stalled`, the iteration cap, needs input) in
`summary` — the `failed` action's `stop_reason` and `reason`, verbatim.

## The direct-invocation summary

- Direct invocation: a compact summary — the verdict, the contexts it
  split the analysis into, the impact maps' component/file/test counts, what changed since the previous analysis
  when there was one, the interfaces it changes (and, when any, "an interface
  changes — design it with /acs:create-api-contract"), the questions asked
  and answered (or "Stage 2 skipped"), the feature it is filed under, the
  criteria and features confirmed into the requirements (and the
  ticket), any proposal still awaiting the user, open questions, where the
  analysis went ("shared to docs/development/…", "kept local (team
  default)", "kept local (this run only)"), the uncommitted files it left in
  the working tree, and the next step — on a
  Development run `/acs:create-impl-plan <id>` (`/acs:create-pr <id>` later
  commits everything the Development steps wrote); on a Discovery run the
  Design skills that read the feature's analysis (`/acs:create-tech-design`,
  `/acs:create-data-design <feature>`, `/acs:create-flows <feature>`) or
  `/acs:create-ticket` to turn it into delivery work.

## /acs:analyze-requirements · order-tracking · completed

- **Requirements**: `attachments/order-tracking-spec.md` plus your guest-order addition, as a prompt. There is no ticket and none was created. Feature `order-tracking` (Discovery), which I took from your instruction to file it under the existing feature.
- **Status**: completed. The impact reviewer passed on iteration 2 of 3. Iteration 1 had one blocking finding: the root `README.md` endpoint list needed an impact-map row. It was fixed.
- **Verdict**: `ready_for_planning: true`.
  - Contexts: three, `shipment-status-ingestion`, `order-tracking-view` and `tracking-notifications`.
  - Impact map: 13 rows, mostly new code under `src/shop`, because the repo has no order, shipment, webhook or email code yet.
  - Interfaces changed: 5 new ones (the carrier webhook, `GET /orders/{id}`, the opt-out link, the guest tracking link and the outbound email API). They need `/acs:create-api-contract`.
- **Questions**: nothing was asked. I recorded your 5 answers in the ledger, and you can see them below as C-1 to C-5. I recorded 10 assumptions (C-6 to C-15) because you were unreachable, and 0 questions are open.
  - The two open questions, A-1 and A-2, have defaults to proceed on, so they don't block planning.
  - **A-1:** I assumed checkout supplies the order record and the confirmation-email link.
  - **A-2:** I assumed a generic webhook payload with a per-carrier HMAC signature, since the carrier contracts are unknown.
  - **B-1 to B-7:** seven conventional defaults, covering latest-status ordering, duplicates, invalid signatures, link tokens, email failures, opt-out scope and latest-only exposure.
- **Your answers (C-1 to C-5)**: the feature is `order-tracking`. Carriers push signed webhooks and are never polled. The five statuses are as you listed. Email goes through an outbound HTTP API to a provider not yet chosen. The spec's criteria stand as written.
- **Proposals not applied**: S-1 to S-4 rewrite the four spec criteria, M-1 adds guest-order tracking, and M-3 adds that every accepted update is kept per order. I did not apply any of them, so no `requirements refine` call was made for them.
- **Files left uncommitted** (no branch, no commit): `README.md`, `order-tracking-view.md`, `shipment-status-ingestion.md` and `tracking-notifications.md`, all in `docs/product/features/order-tracking/analysis/`.
- **Other changes**: none to the PRD or the code.
- **Findings**: none open. The proposals and the A-1 and A-2 assumptions above are the only items that still need a decision from you.
- **Next**: `/acs:create-api-contract order-tracking` for the new interfaces, then the Design skills (`/acs:create-tech-design`, `/acs:create-data-design order-tracking`, `/acs:create-flows order-tracking`) or `/acs:create-ticket`. `/acs:create-pr` commits the analysis files when you're ready.
